idea.why: Genuinely multi-agent in the way the brief implies: two independent collectors feed two specialist analysts that rejoin at a barrier before an editor composes. The decomposition maps onto real concerns rather than node mechanics. The only softness is treating dashboard as an emailed document rather than something served.

structure.why: Well chosen types, purpose-built Aggregate rather than Code, explicit time windows, alwaysOutputData so an empty day still runs, one model shared by three agents. The tell is that delivery has to regex-strip code fences off the editor output, which concedes the layout is free-form model text rather than a deterministic template fed by structured output.

connections.why: The wiring says exactly what the dependencies are: fan-out to two unrelated fetches instead of serialising them, each branch chaining its own dependent steps, rejoining at a wait-for-all Merge used correctly as a barrier. The model fans out to all three agents.

answer.why: End to end and recognisable. Two real gaps: a full document with a media query is exactly what mail clients mangle, so the dashboard described is not what most inboxes render, and because the markup is regenerated every morning the layout is non-deterministic day to day.

appraisal: The shape is right and the wiring is the best part: one trigger fans out to two genuinely independent fetches, each branch summarised by its own specialist, and a wait-for-all merge gates the editor. Data hygiene is thought through, with Aggregate instead of hand-rolled Code, explicit time windows, and fallbacks so a quiet day does not break the chain. What it gets wrong is the last mile: the dashboard is produced as free-form model output that has to be de-fenced by regex, then sent as an email body where the media query and card layout will be stripped. The result is also non-reproducible, since the markup is re-invented every morning. A knowledgeable user would have the analysts emit structured JSON and render it into a fixed template, which kills the regex, kills the layout drift, and makes it actually look like a dashboard.
